items.title: Jon Weber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 2, 2012
items.q: But when you follow it, and Frank Zappa says exactly the same thing.

ctx.x: No. No. No. Well if you’re playing — okay — if you’re playing Beethoven’s ninth symphony yes. There’s a wrong note there. If you’re jazz — there was a great TED feature that Stefon Harris did called “There Are No Wrong Notes on the Bandstand” meaning in a jazz combo setting they were playing kind of an F suspension thing together with a little quartet. Stefon was playing vibes and there was a pianist and a drummer and a bass player, and he asked the pianist, he said, “F sharp” which is about as harsh as it gets…
of a situation I don’t think so. And in most situations I would say no. I would say a wrong note is a rarity. I’ll compromise that much.
